page: Microsoft Azure E48ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache specifications consist of 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 463.87 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 200.05 GB/sec. Multi-core compute capabilities are strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21904.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 99340.45. Database operations are highly efficient, with Passmark database operations scoring in the top 10% at 37055.11 and Redis SET operations processing 89.22 million operations per second. Single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1692.0. Large LLM inference workloads represent a performance tradeoff, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 25% at 6.91 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48ps_v6 offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The dedicated ARM core architecture provides predictable performance scaling for multi-threaded tasks. This server is highly suited for memory-optimized workloads, including relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, large-scale software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
